findings.reason: two opposite implementations both satisfy the prose (immediate classification can kill a run whose probe merely failed once, while a bound needs a history the plan never says `sweep` records for non-answers), so the node's done-when and its guard differ by whoever reads it.
findings.text: the deliverable says "The producer-gone rule applies only to a probe that answered" and defines producer-gone as all three clauses, then says a non-answering probe with no live process and no exit record "is producer-gone as well"; but the stillness clause (`wait_probe_history` recording "each observed probe value and its time") cannot be evaluated for a probe that produced no value, so the node is left to choose between classifying on the first unanswered sweep and inventing a bound and a history entry the plan does not specify.

findings.reason: the section exists to stop a dead run reading as live, and as written it would make a live run read as dead after fifteen minutes of a still probe, which is a worse failure than the one it repairs.
findings.text: clause 1, "No process of the run is alive … read through `process_liveness.process_alive` and `recovery_liveness._live_descendant`, never a second process check", is satisfied by an unresolved reading: `process_alive` returns `None` when the pointer records no pid, `_live_descendant` returns `False` when the child list is unreadable, and the existing `_process_reading` (recovery_liveness.py:437-461) deliberately calls that state "liveness unknown" rather than death, because a stored answer from another host is not an observation; the plan forbids the second check that would tell these apart, so a live run on a host whose liveness cannot be proven is classified producer-gone.

findings.reason: an unguarded branch is exactly the case this plan's own controls exist to catch, and the revision added it without one.
findings.text: arm 4 now ends "With no exit record and no live process, the run is producer-gone", but the two declared negative controls cover only the process-liveness clause (file-wait arm) and the scheduler-job clause (`squeue` arm); neither removes the no-exit-record routing, so a node could omit that branch entirely and still pass every arm and both controls.

findings.reason: a node runs every named arm regardless of the count, so the miscount changes no behaviour.
findings.text: "Done when … shows four things" introduces a list of five bullets.
